description: The hand pump near the primary school in Bero has been broken for three months, families walk 2km to fetch water every morning.
Our village well has gone dry since February and the tanker only comes once a week, that too not on a fixed day.
Sewage water is mixing into the drinking water pipeline near the market and people are getting stomach illness.
The overhead tank built two years ago has never been connected to any pipeline, it is standing empty.
Groundwater has dropped so much that our borewell now needs to go 300 feet, small farmers cannot afford this.
The check dam on the seasonal river has a large crack and water leaks out before the dry season starts.
Water supply in our colony comes only for 20 minutes at 5am, working people cannot collect it.
The village pond that cattle drink from has been encroached and filled with construction debris.
Iron content in our tubewell water is very high, it stains clothes yellow and tastes metallic.
Rainwater harvesting structures were built at the school but the pipes were never fitted, all the water is wasted.
The main water pipeline burst near the bus stand ten days ago and thousands of litres flow into the drain daily.
Fluoride in our drinking water is causing brown teeth in children across the whole panchayat.
Only one hand pump serves 400 households in our tola and there is fighting in the queue every morning.
The canal that irrigates our block has been silted up for years and water does not reach the tail-end villages.
The municipal tanker driver demands money before filling our drums, otherwise he goes to another lane.
The primary health centre has had no doctor posted since April, people travel to Ranchi for basic treatment.
Our ASHA worker has no blood pressure machine or weighing scale, she measures everything by guesswork.
The ambulance for our block has been under repair for five months, pregnant women are carried on cots.
A vaccination camp was announced but the vaccine carrier had no ice packs so the session was cancelled.
There is no functioning cold chain in our PHC, the refrigerator has been dead since last summer.
Dengue cases have risen sharply in our ward this month and no fogging has been done at all.
The sub-centre building has no toilet and no water, the nurse cannot conduct deliveries there.
Medicines prescribed at the government hospital are never in stock, we always have to buy them outside.
Sickle cell anaemia is common in our community but no screening has ever been done in this district.
Elderly patients have to climb two floors for the OPD because the hospital lift has never worked.
Mental health support is completely absent, families with a mentally ill member have nowhere to go.
Malnutrition among under-fives in our anganwadi area is visible but supplementary nutrition has not arrived for two months.
Snakebite victims in our forest village die on the way because no antivenom is stocked nearby.
The only lab technician for four villages left last year and blood tests have stopped since then.
Tuberculosis patients stop treatment midway because the DOTS centre is 18km away with no transport.
Our government school has 180 children and only two teachers, one of them is on deputation elsewhere.
The school roof leaks badly in monsoon and classes are suspended for weeks every year.
A computer lab was set up under a scheme but there is no electricity connection and no trained teacher.
Girls drop out after class 8 because the nearest high school is 12km away and there is no transport.
Textbooks for this academic year have still not arrived and it is already October.
Mid-day meal quality is very poor, children refuse to eat and many go home hungry.
There is no library or reading material in our village school beyond the prescribed textbooks.
Children in our tribal hamlet are taught only in Hindi which they do not speak at home, so they fall behind.
The anganwadi centre runs from a shed with no floor, small children sit on bare mud.
Science practicals have never been conducted in our school because the lab has no equipment.
Students who passed class 12 have no guidance about college admission or scholarship forms.
Our school was merged with another one 6km away and small children now walk along the highway.
Online classes were announced during exams but most families in our village have no smartphone.
The only teacher who taught mathematics retired last year and no replacement has been posted.
Attendance registers are marked full but half the enrolled children have not come to school in months.
Wild elephants raid our paddy fields every night in harvest season and we have no protection.
Soil testing has never been done in our block so farmers apply fertiliser purely by guesswork.
There is no cold storage within 60km so our tomato crop rots before it reaches the mandi.
Seeds supplied by the cooperative last season had very poor germination and many farmers lost the crop.
A pest attack has destroyed the standing maize crop and no agriculture officer has visited.
Farmers here still broadcast seed by hand because no seed drill is available for hire in the block.
Crop insurance claims from two years ago have still not been settled for our village.
The lift irrigation scheme built for our fields has a burnt motor that nobody has repaired.
Stray cattle destroy standing crops at night and farmers take turns staying awake in the fields.
We grow good quality turmeric but there is no processing unit so we sell it raw at a very low price.
Erratic rainfall has made our traditional sowing calendar useless and nobody advises us on new timing.
The mandi is 45km away and traders at the village gate pay us half the government rate.
Our farm ponds silted up after two monsoons and there is no machinery to desilt them.
Kisan Credit Card applications from our panchayat have been pending at the bank for over a year.
Fodder shortage in summer forces us to sell cattle cheaply every year before the rains.
A factory upstream releases coloured effluent into the river and the fish have disappeared.
Garbage is dumped and burned at the edge of our colony every evening and the smoke enters our homes.
Illegal sand mining from the riverbed is eroding the bank near our village.
Coal dust from the passing trucks covers our crops and houses throughout the day.
The forest patch beside our village is being cleared without any notice or consultation.
Air quality near the stone crusher is so bad that children have persistent coughs.
Untreated hospital waste is being thrown in the open ground behind the health centre.
The pond in our village has turned green and foul smelling after sewage was diverted into it.
Old mining pits near our settlement are unfenced and fill with contaminated water in the monsoon.
Trees along the district road were felled for widening and nothing was planted in return.
Noise from the crusher unit runs all night and nobody in the nearby houses sleeps properly.
Fly ash from the thermal plant settles on our fields and yields have dropped every year.
The municipal dump site has no segregation and waste pickers including children work there barehanded.
A wetland where migratory birds came every winter is being filled in for housing plots.
Open defecation along the canal bank continues because the built toilets have no water supply.
Power cuts last eight to ten hours daily in our village, mostly during evening study time.
The transformer for our hamlet burnt out six weeks ago and has not been replaced.
Solar street lights installed two years ago have all stopped working, the batteries were never replaced.
Voltage fluctuation is so severe that motors and appliances burn out regularly.
Twenty houses in our tola have still not received an electricity connection at all.
Electric poles in our lane are bamboo and the wires hang low over the walking path.
LPG refills have to be collected from 25km away, so most families still cook on firewood.
The biogas plant built under a scheme has been non functional since the first year.
Electricity bills arrive with wildly wrong readings and there is no way to get them corrected locally.
The solar pump sanctioned for our irrigation group was never installed though the file shows it complete.
Our school has an electricity connection but no wiring inside the classrooms.
Frequent tripping damages the motor at the community borewell.
Streetlights on the approach road have never been switched on since installation.
Households here spend a large part of their income on kerosene because supply is unreliable.
The feeder line supplying our block is overloaded and fails every time there is light rain.
The road to our village becomes impassable mud for four months of the year.
There is a deep open drain along the main lane with no cover, a child fell in last month.
The culvert on the approach road collapsed in the last monsoon and has not been rebuilt.
Our ward has no public toilet and the nearest one is locked most of the day.
Garbage is not collected from our street so residents dump it at the corner instead.
The footbridge over the railway line has broken steps and no railing on one side.
The bus stand has no shelter, passengers including women wait in the sun and rain.
Potholes on the main market road have caused several two wheeler accidents this year.
Storm water drains were built without slope so water stagnates instead of flowing away.
The community hall built five years ago has no doors or windows and is unusable.
Our locality floods every monsoon because the nala was narrowed by construction.
There is no crossing or signal near the school gate on the state highway.
Street names and house numbering do not exist so ambulances and deliveries cannot find addresses.
The village crematorium has no roof and cremations are impossible during rain.
A half built overbridge has been abandoned for three years and blocks the old route.
Our village school has no ramp, my daughter uses a wheelchair and cannot get into the classroom.
The panchayat office is on the first floor with narrow stairs, disabled people cannot reach it.
There is no disabled friendly toilet anywhere in our block headquarters.
Blind students in our area have no access to braille books or screen reader devices.
Disability certificates require three visits to the district hospital which is unaffordable for us.
The new bus shelter has a high step that elderly and disabled passengers cannot climb.
Deaf children in our village have never had access to a sign language teacher.
Public buildings here have no tactile paving or handrails of any kind.
My son needs a prosthetic limb but the nearest fitting centre is in another state.
Wheelchairs distributed under a scheme are the wrong size for children and lie unused.
Government forms and notices are only in printed Hindi, visually impaired citizens cannot read them independently.
The ration shop has three steps and no ramp so my father cannot collect his own entitlement.
There is no special educator for children with intellectual disability in the entire block.
Hearing aids given two years ago have no battery replacement available anywhere nearby.
The new community centre was built without any accessible entrance despite the guidelines.
My pension has not been credited for seven months and nobody at the office gives a clear answer.
Caste certificate applications from our village have been pending for over a year without reason.
The ration dealer marks our fingerprint but gives less grain than what is recorded.
Land records show a wrong name and correcting it requires repeated trips to the tehsil office.
The panchayat has not held a gram sabha meeting in two years despite the requirement.
Our MGNREGA wages for work done in April have still not been paid.
Applications submitted online show status pending forever and no contact number works.
The block office staff demand money for issuing an income certificate.
Beneficiary lists for the housing scheme were never displayed publicly as required.
A death certificate for my mother has been refused three times over minor spelling issues.
Our RTI application was ignored completely and no response came within the time limit.
Aadhaar linking errors have removed several genuine families from the ration list.
The village revenue official visits only once a month and is never available when needed.
Scholarship applications for tribal students were rejected in bulk without any reason given.
Funds sanctioned for our ward last financial year lapsed without any work being done.
Women in our self help group weave baskets but have no market beyond the weekly haat.
Most young men from our village migrate to Surat because there is no work here after harvest.
Our handloom weavers get yarn at a high price from middlemen and earn very little per piece.
Tribal families collect tendu leaves but the traders fix the rate and we have no bargaining power.
The skill training centre opened here trains only in tailoring which everyone already knows.
Our fishermen cooperative has no ice box or transport so the catch is sold cheap locally.
Bamboo craftsmen in our village have no design input and their products no longer sell.
Banks refuse loans to landless workers here so they depend on moneylenders.
Dairy farmers here have no chilling centre so milk must be sold within two hours.
MGNREGA work is available only 20 days a year in our panchayat instead of the promised hundred.
Poultry rearing was promoted but no veterinary support exists and birds die in large numbers.
Honey collectors in our forest area have no processing or bottling facility.
Our women's group got a sewing machine grant but nobody trained them to maintain the machines.
Migrant workers returning from cities have no local employment option and no skill certification.
Lac cultivation is traditional here but yields fell and no extension support is available.
